findings.diagnosis: The scorer has a leftward cut bias that often isolates predicates, auxiliaries, negation, or required complements onto very short pieces, producing standalone fragments whose meaning is reversed or incomplete when joined later.
findings.evidence: Shows in 9 cases (en_us_733, en_us_738, en_us_845, en_us_1116, en_us_990, en_us_538, en_us_655, en_us_1567, en_us_1081): all keep an early cut that separates a verb/negation or its complement and a single later cut with high contradiction zeroes the H_set.

edit.text: Do not cut so a very short fragment (≈≤4 words) contains only a predicate/auxiliary/negation or its particle while its required complement, object, or licensing head appears later; prefer keeping verb + its complements and scope-bearing operators together.

findings.diagnosis: The scorer underweights high post-cut contradiction: positions that leave a later fragment which, on its own, strongly contradicts or overturns the earlier fragment are not being penalized enough.
findings.evidence: Appears in the same 9 cases where a single policy cut has very high 'contra' and causes the set to fail (policy_worst_contra ≈0.8–0.99); targets avoid those cuts and obtain much higher H_set.

edit.text: When the material after a cut has a high probability of contradicting the prior fragment (contra > ~0.5), mark that cut unsafe and drop its rank substantially — such high contra should heavily lower the cut’s score regardless of moderate cohesion.
